newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natural gas companies brace for consolidation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natural gas companies brace for consolidation.

text.p: The annual Howard Weil energy conference opened on Monday with news of the Mesa Inc /Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co merger, leaving executives buzzing about a new round of mergers ahead for the natural gas industry.

Natural gas company executives talked openly about potential mergers on the horizon as the industry braces for consolidation being driven by cost-cutting and looming deregulation of the electric industry.
"This is only the start," Parker & Parsley Executive Vice President Tim Leach said.

The Texas-based companies unveiled plans to merge and form Pioneer Natural Resources Co, a $2.9 billion company that would be the nation's third largest independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company.

Pioneer would have more than 3.7 trillion cubic feet of natural gas equivalent reserves and daily production of more than 64,000 barrels of crude oil and natural gas liquids and 459 million cubic feet of natural gas, the companies said.

The deal marked the latest chapter in Mesa's turnaround, and came as executives with rival companies have been quietly engaged in their own preliminary merger talks and taking steps to hold down debt levels to keep merger options open.
"We want to have the capacity to make major acquisitions," said Williams Cos Inc Chairman Keith Bailey, adding that he has been actively seeking acquisitions to expand his company's energy business.

Considered one of the most attractive merger candidates among the major pipeline companies, Williams is focused on major metropolitan markets -- particularly in the Northeast corridor -- to form partnerships with electric utilities, he said.

Drawing from a blueprint of its limited liability partnership with Boston Edison Co, Bailey said the company is seeking to form similar ventures with utilities to reach retail and wholesale customers nationwide.

"We would like to do similar things in other regions of the country and we do have discussions underway to accomplish that," he said. "About the only region we see that is not interested in moving too fast is the Mid-Atlantic."
Consolidated Natural Gas Co Chairman George Davidson said his company also has been approached about a possible business combination, but "could be a player on either side" of a merger.
"It won't be a frenzy, but I think it will be done in an orderly way," he said of a wave of mergers on the horizon between electric utilities and natural gas producers and pipeline companies.
